document_or_genre: British Library Royal MS 12 G IV
attested_feature: An alphabetical herbal synonym list, a work on weights and measures with medicinal qualities, and Latin, French and English recipes coexist in one codex.
working_relevance: Supports a mixed practical register of learned substance heads, process qualities, fractions, quantities and commands.
scope_limit: Architecture analogy only; it identifies no Voynich sign, language, ingredient or unit.

attested_feature: Roughly 250 medical recipes, the Antidotarium Nicolai, a glossary of simples and herbs, and a De gradibus extract share the manuscript.
working_relevance: Near-period evidence that recipe instructions, degree ladders and learned drug-name glossaries can coexist in one workshop book.
scope_limit: Does not prove that the Voynich manuscript is this genre or uses the same vocabulary.

attested_feature: A botanical glossary and about 130 recipes accompany the Antidotarium Nicolai; catalogued recipe lines combine Recipe, drug names, dram signs and Roman quantities.
working_relevance: Supports compact take or add commands directly bound to named material and dose values.
scope_limit: Does not map q, y, or, aiin or another Voynich component to Latin.

attested_feature: The manuscript contains direct Recipe formulae and quantities expressed with equal amounts and grains.
working_relevance: Supports the local sequence of material class, fraction or portion, cardinal value and a small medicinal weight.
scope_limit: Does not decide the tolg reader dispute between grain, handful and a joined form.

attested_feature: Liber graduum, Quid pro quo, medicinal recipes and an Arabic-Latin herbal-name glossary coexist.
working_relevance: Strong analogue for productive technical qualifiers beside memorized composite-drug or ingredient heads.
scope_limit: Does not select Arabic, Latin or a particular nomenclator for Voynichese.

document_or_genre: British Library Harley MS 2558, f.12v; Thomas Fayreford De saporibus et gradibus
attested_feature: A compact work on tastes and medicinal degrees was copied into a practical medical collection in the target period.
working_relevance: Supports hot, cold, dry and moist values combined with ordered degree notation and finished preparation states around 1420.
scope_limit: Supports only the information type, not the individual proposed mappings.

document_or_genre: University of Nottingham palaeography guide to letter forms and abbreviations
attested_feature: Frequent words were heavily abbreviated, letters could be omitted, and minim sequences were context-dependent.
working_relevance: Makes cthor oraiin, kchs and daiiirchy legitimate manual-reader controls rather than newly invented Voynich words.
scope_limit: Does not authorize arbitrary segmentation or prove that any alternate reading is semantically correct.
